builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Quantizing Diffusion LLMs under Parallel Decoding: Commitment Risk and the Parallelism Tax
summary: DECAL replaces standard layer-wise W4A4 post-training calibration (performed under fixed-step samplers) with commitment-risk-reweighted calibration measured on the deployed cached parallel decoder, plus an argmax-preserving commit temperature that recovers the extra forward passes quantization causes. It costs an offline commitment-risk measurement on the deployed decoder and a small change to the commit rule; memory footprint stays at W4A4 and no retraining is required. It can fail if the production decoder configuration drifts from the one used for calibration, if the model is not a dLLM served with threshold-based parallel decoding (making the method inapplicable), or if forced-commitment behavior on the reader's tasks differs from LLaDA/Dream benchmarks.
rationale: The method is directly relevant if the reader serves diffusion LLMs (LLaDA/Dream) quantized to W4A4 under cached threshold-based parallel decoding, but it is workload-specific and must be validated on the reader's own decoder and tasks before adoption.
technique: Commitment-risk-aware W4A4 calibration for diffusion LLMs

claims.statement: DECAL replaces standard layer-wise W4A4 post-training calibration (performed under fixed-step samplers) with commitment-risk-reweighted calibration measured on the deployed cached parallel decoder, plus an argmax-preserving commit temperature that recovers the extra forward passes quantization causes. It costs an offline commitment-risk measurement on the deployed decoder and a small change to the commit rule; memory footprint stays at W4A4 and no retraining is required. It can fail if the production decoder configuration drifts from the one used for calibration, if the model is not a dLLM served with threshold-based parallel decoding (making the method inapplicable), or if forced-commitment behavior on the reader's tasks differs from LLaDA/Dream benchmarks.

DECAL attains the best average accuracy among W4A4 methods on LLaDA and Dream under the deployed cached parallel decoder, with lower run-to-run variance than the closest existing calibration method; no multiplicative improvement factor is reported.
